rationale: Verb appearing four times on this page (lines 4, 9, 13, 20) in contexts of speech-proclamation paralleling ⲧⲁϣⲉⲁⲓϣ 'proclaim.' Likely Lycopolitan reflex of ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon, tell' in transferred sense 'declare, make known.' Distinct from ⲧⲁϣⲉⲁⲓϣ (public proclamation) and from ⲉⲓⲡⲉ as related to ⲣⲉⲛ 'name' (which would yield 'to name' — also possible).

Lycopolitan ⲗⲱϫϩ used here in transferred sense 'constrain, restrict' (line 15: 'the world has constrained me'). Distinct from accumulated ⲗⲱⲭⲍ̄ 'defile, pollute,' though same root. Captures the soteriological sense of Mani's restricted preaching.
Greek καί ταῦτα adopted as Coptic discourse-connective. Standard transliteration. Functions to introduce a corollary clause: 'moreover/and these things being so.'

Hybrid Greek-Coptic compound: ὑπο- 'under' + ⲥⲉϫⲉ 'speak.' Verbal counterpart to the agent-noun ⲍⲩⲡⲟⲁⲉϫⲉ 'counselor' (in glossary). In negation 'they did not heed me' = they did not bow themselves to my speech.

Lycopolitan 1sg perfect of ⲃⲛ̄ (= Sahidic ⲉⲓⲛⲉ / ϥⲓ 'bring, bear, carry'). Parallel form to line 8 ⲛⲧⲁⲃⲛ̄ 'that I bring.' Used here in 'I bore necessity' (line 25) — Mani enduring perilous compulsion during his sea voyage.

Adverbial usage of the qualitative ⲙⲏϩ 'be full' from ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill.' In context (line 10) modifies ⲉⲧⲁϣⲉⲁⲓϣ 'is proclaimed' — 'the mystery that is fully proclaimed in the living truth.' Could alternatively be reflexive 'itself.'
